description: Format several sources at once as one works cited list, alphabetised by the first author's family name in APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago author date or Harvard, numbered in citation order in IEEE, or as one BibTeX block in the order you give the sources. A source with no author is alphabetised by its title. Inputs: sources (an array of objects, each with the same fields as format_citation: type, title and optional authors, year, container, publisher, city, edition, editors, translators, volume, issue, pages, doi, url, date_text, accessed, institution, degree, repository and report_number), dois (a list of DOIs to look up on Crossref), isbns (a list of ISBNs to look up on Open Library), urls (a list of web addresses to fetch and cite as websites) and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad, harvard, ieee or bibtex). Give sources, dois, isbns, urls or any mix, up to 50 lookups in one call. If one lookup fails the reply is an error that names it. Example prompt: "Put these three sources into an APA works cited list: a journal article by Smith and Jones from 2020, a book by Cormen from 2009 and a website from example.edu."

dois.description: DOIs to look up on Crossref and add to the list, each one a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link.

isbns.description: ISBNs to look up on Open Library and add to the list as books. Dashes are fine.

sources.description: The sources for the list. Each one takes the same fields as format_citation, so a journal article, a book, a website, a chapter, a thesis, a report, a dataset and a preprint can share one list. Optional when you give dois, isbns or urls.

city.description: Publisher city, used by Chicago for books.

container.description: Journal name, the book title for a chapter, or website name. Required for a journal article and for a chapter, since without it the citation would be missing the work it appears in.

date_text.description: Website date as you want it shown, like "2026, October 14" for APA or "14 Oct. 2026" for MLA.

degree.description: The degree of a thesis, like "Ph.D.".

editors.description: Editors of a book or a chapter, same shape as authors. When a book has editors and no authors, they take the author's place in the citation.

institution.description: The university or organisation behind a thesis, a report or a dataset.

report_number.description: The number of a report or a standard.

repository.description: Where a preprint was posted, like arXiv.

translators.description: Translators of a book, same shape as authors.

style.description: Citation style. Aliases such as APA, MLA 9 and Chicago are accepted. Valid styles: apa7, mla9, chicago-ad (Chicago author date), harvard, ieee and bibtex.

urls.description: Web addresses to fetch and add to the list as websites. Each one a full URL like https://example.edu/study.

name: format_bibliography
title: Format a works cited list
